title: Best Fridge Freezers UK
short: Fridge freezers compared on real lab-measured temperature stability and running costs, from budget 60cm models to premium French Door and American-style units.
intro: A fridge freezer's real test is whether it holds a stable temperature day after day, not its marketing spec. This guide compares fridge freezers tested by Trusted Reviews in their Home Technology Lab, loaded with freezer blocks and monitored with temperature probes over two weeks, with power use measured to estimate real running costs.

products.name: Bespoke AI Family Hub RS90F66BETEU
products.best_for: Buyers with the budget for a large, feature-packed American-style fridge freezer
products.key_spec: 319L fridge, 225L freezer, auto-open doors, 21.5in touchscreen hub, only 60cm deep
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found spot-on temperature control, with the fridge averaging 3.51°C against a 4°C target and the freezer averaging -19°C, both with very little variation top to bottom. Auto-open doors respond to a hand wave and a large touchscreen doubles as a family organiser, though the Bixby voice integration for opening doors proved hit and miss.
pros: Large touchscreen hub genuinely useful for families
cons: Bixby voice control for doors is hit and miss
products.search: Samsung Bespoke AI Family Hub RS90F66BETEU

products.name: RB3K330SAIC
products.best_for: Buyers who want an integrated look without losing capacity
products.key_spec: 215L fridge, 115L freezer, KitchenFit flush design, ConnectLife smart app, C-rated
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this shallow 60cm-wide model gives far more capacity than a typical integrated fridge freezer while still sitting flush with kitchen counters. Temperature control was very stable, with the fridge just 0.63°C warmer than its 4°C target, and the ConnectLife app warns of problems like a door left open, though door pockets feel slightly inflexible.
pros: Good capacity for a flush-fit model
cons: Top of fridge runs a little warmer than middle and bottom

products.name: RQ768N4GVE
products.best_for: Buyers who want French Door capacity in a flush-fit footprint
products.key_spec: 381L fridge, 2x 105L freezer compartments, 60cm deep, vacuum drawer, convertible freezer zone
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this KitchenFit French Door model gives full-size capacity while needing just 3mm clearance on either side. Performance was excellent, with the fridge averaging 4.23°C and the freezer -18.22°C, both with minimal fluctuation, and one freezer compartment can convert to extra fridge space, though there's no smart app or water dispenser.
pros: Only as deep as a standard kitchen counter
One freezer section converts to fridge space

products.name: CNG7603VPX
products.best_for: Buyers who want maximum flexibility from a standard-width fridge freezer
products.key_spec: 249L fridge, 106L freezer, convertible freezer-to-fridge section, HarvestFresh LED drawers, B-rated
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this standard 60cm model full of surprises, with the bottom freezer section convertible into extra fridge space and HarvestFresh LED technology in the drawers designed to preserve fresh food longer. Temperature control was spot-on at exactly 4°C in the fridge and -18.28°C in the freezer, making it a B-rated appliance costing just £18.79 a year to run.
pros: Freezer section converts to extra fridge space
cons: Top fridge shelf could be hard to reach

products.name: MBsddi 9024 plus BioFresh NoFrost
products.best_for: Buyers who want the best possible temperature stability and interior design
products.key_spec: 354L French Door fridge, 219L freezer, soft-close BioFresh drawers, built-in ice maker
products.summary: Trusted Reviews called performance exceptional, with the fridge averaging 4.03°C and the freezer a steady -19.36°C with very little variation between readings. Soft-close telescopic drawers slide out smoothly and frost never accumulates so manual defrosting is never needed, though it's expensive and the ice maker is a little untidy.
cons: Ice maker is a bit untidy

products.name: Series 8 RM70F67RDR
products.best_for: Buyers who want a large French Door fridge freezer with genuinely low running costs
products.key_spec: 414L full-width fridge, 255L freezer, AI Hybrid Cooling with Peltier element, D-rated
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found AI Hybrid Cooling, which pairs a Peltier element with traditional cooling, delivers excellent stability: the fridge ran slightly colder than set at 3.07°C with just +/-0.26°C fluctuation. At an estimated £40.30 a year to run, that's almost unheard of for a fridge this size, though it's expensive to buy and skips a water or ice dispenser.
pros: Unusually low running costs for its size

products.name: H-Fridge 700 Maxi HSC918EWXK
products.best_for: Buyers who want French Door style and space without the premium price
products.key_spec: 363L fridge, 201L freezer across six drawers, built-in water dispenser, no filter
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this proves French Door style doesn't have to be expensive, with a large 363-litre fridge and a front water dispenser fed from an internal tank. Fridge temperature control was very good for the price at an average 3.8°C, though the freezer's six drawers all share one compartment rather than being separately controllable.
pros: Great value for a French Door model
Excellent fridge temperature control for the price

products.name: H-Combi 300 HONCQ2T618EWK
products.best_for: Buyers on a tight budget who still want reliable, stable cooling
products.key_spec: 235L fridge, 120L freezer, fridge-only temperature control, E-rated
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this exceptionally well-priced model gets all the basics right, with a flexible 235-litre fridge and a simple, functional 120-litre freezer. The fridge ran 1.21°C colder than its set point in testing, a good result, though there's no temperature control for the freezer section and running costs are a little higher at this budget.
cons: No temperature control for the freezer
Relatively expensive to run for its size

guide.q: Freestanding, integrated or French Door: which style should I choose?
guide.a: A freestanding model gives you the most capacity for your money and is easiest to move house with. An integrated fridge freezer like the Hotpoint HTC20T322UK blends into your kitchen units but usually sacrifices some capacity. A French Door model like the Liebherr or Samsung Series 8 here puts the whole fridge at eye level across the top, which some buyers find more practical than a side-by-side layout.

guide.q: How much does the energy rating actually affect running costs?
guide.a: Trusted Reviews' testing found real running costs ranged from around £18.79 a year for the B-rated Beko here to over £70 for the premium Liebherr, so the rating band is a genuinely useful shortcut. Comparing the cost per litre of storage space, rather than the total yearly figure, is the fairest way to compare models of different sizes.

guide.q: Does a flush-fit or 'KitchenFit' model really give up much capacity?
guide.a: Not necessarily. Trusted Reviews found the Hisense RB3K330SAIC and RQ768N4GVE here, both only 60cm deep to sit flush with kitchen counters, still offered significantly more space than a true integrated model, making them a good middle ground between a built-in look and freestanding capacity.

guide.q: Is a convertible fridge/freezer section worth having?
guide.a: Yes, if your storage needs change through the year. The Beko CNG7603VPX here lets you convert its freezer section into extra fridge space, useful for hosting a party or over Christmas, while the Hisense RQ768N4GVE offers a similar convertible zone in one of its two freezer compartments.
